questions.q: Why do duplicate Accounts and Contacts pile up in a long-running Salesforce org, per this lesson?
options: Search is imperfect and creating a new record is often faster than finding the existing one, so reps and imports create duplicates without malice
Salesforce automatically duplicates every record every quarter
Duplicate Rules are turned on by default and create copies intentionally
Accounts can only be created once per calendar year, forcing workarounds
questions.explain: Duplicates are usually a byproduct of imperfect search and fast record creation, not malice or a system bug.

questions.q: What does this query actually catch: SELECT Name, COUNT(Id) recordCount FROM Account GROUP BY Name HAVING COUNT(Id) > 1?
options: Only exact-name duplicates — it would miss 'Acme Corp' vs. 'Acme Corporation'
Every possible duplicate, including near-matches and typos
Duplicate Contacts, not Accounts
Records with missing required fields
questions.explain: GROUP BY/HAVING on Name only finds exact string matches, which is why fuzzy matching tools are covered next lesson.

questions.q: Why can a Contact end up in Salesforce with no Email even though Email looks 'required' on the page layout?
options: Page-layout required fields aren't enforced at the database level, so records from Data Loader or an integration can skip them
Email is never actually a real Salesforce field
SOQL blocks queries on empty fields by default
Contacts created via the UI always bypass page layout rules
questions.explain: 'Required' at the page-layout level only constrains that specific UI path, not every way a record can be created.

questions.q: What makes a record 'stale' or 'orphaned', per this lesson's description?
options: It was accurate when created but no longer reflects reality because nobody maintains it over time
It was entered incorrectly from the very first moment it was created
It has too many related Activities logged against it
It was created by an integration rather than a human user
questions.explain: Staleness is about decay over time — accurate at creation, wrong now — not an entry error.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why are CRM data quality problems described as 'structural' rather than accidental?
options: They arise from how people actually use Salesforce day to day, not from occasional carelessness
They are caused by a specific Salesforce software bug that has never been patched
They only occur in orgs with fewer than 10 users
They are intentionally built into every Salesforce license
questions.explain: The lesson frames duplicates, inconsistent values, missing fields, and staleness as predictable outcomes of everyday usage patterns.
